title: State Complexity of Exact Randomization Inference under Stochastic Pocock-Simon Minimization

proof_attempt_summary: Two D-1 proposal versions developed an exact suffix-clipped randomization-state package. The second repaired positive-support transition soundness and added a concrete two-factor family in which 2^(B/2) clipped states merge into one labeled-law class, leaving no soundness flags. The package remained letter-tier because the decisive 1988 recursion and 2026 supplement could not be audited and no usable general multifactor criterion was established, so the field-floor run terminated before Stage 0.
tldr: The proposal asks exactly how much history an exact finite-sample randomization calculation must retain under absolute-range stochastic Pocock--Simon minimization. Its candidate answer combines remaining-occurrence clipping, the coarsest support-aware labeled future-law quotient, and a positive-branch rational score DP; it matches the clipping frontier in one factor, proves a two-factor incidence/weight family where \(2^{B/2}\) clipped states collapse to one labeled class, and separates explicit conditional scalar-law growth from general hardness through a binary-score construction with an easy unconditional binomial bypass. The causal exogeneity condition is confined to the sharp-null validity proposition, not the combinatorial DP.
gap: Exact restricted-randomization recursion and generic finite-horizon quotienting are established. What remains unresolved is a suffix-aware state theorem for the declared absolute-range marginal kernel, the precise relation among clipped, labeled-law, and scalar-law states, and sharp design-specific frontiers. Full text needed to clear overlap with MehtaPatelWei1988 and Kojima2026 Supplementary A.2 is inaccessible, so the project does not claim novelty from search absence.
fill: Prove the clipping semiconjugacy, support-aware canonical quotient, and positive-branch exact rational recurrence; separate that design theorem from sharp-null validity; match the one-factor upper frontier; establish the two-factor exponential masking gap; and state all lower bounds in their explicit representation models while retaining the binomial bypass.
